answer: Three beacon nodes ping a new agent and log the round trip times, a fingerprint of where its machine sits. A real agent stays rooted like a willow by a river, its latency steady week after week. Two identities on one server land within 2 milliseconds of each other, like water in the same karst channels underground, so the network flags the pair and demands proof from a different machine. Renting 1,000 machines across 20 regions runs about $4,000 a month plus 12 hours of setup per batch, so the farm pays more than it earns. A fake crowd is a plume of smoke rising from a single chimney.
